glosses: to help

examples.text: Я ему́ помога́л.

glosses: to aid, to assist materially

examples.text: Я дру́гу помога́ю де́ньгами.
examples.translation: I'm helping a friend with money.
examples.english: I'm helping a friend with money.

glosses: to avail, to work (to have the desired effect)

examples.text: Лека́рство помога́ет.

glosses: содействовать чему-либо или способствовать чьей-либо деятельности

examples.text: — Кто же вам помогал зашивать месяц назад? // — Никто не помогал, сам зашил.
На первых порах мама или папа должны помогать ребёнку при выполнении домашнего задания, но не делая за него работу, а лишь подталкивая к правильному решению.

glosses: поддерживать материально, предоставлять деньги или иные средства
излечивать, облегчать, решать проблему

examples.text: У отставного генерал-майора Булдеева разболелись зубы. Он полоскал рот водкой, коньяком, прикладывал к больному зубу табачную копоть, опий, скипидар, керосин, мазал щёку йодом, в ушах у него была вата, смоченная в спирту, но всё это или не помогало, или вызывало тошноту.
Наркологи и психологи говорят… что принудительное лечение не помогает.

translations.source_sense_description: содействовать чему-либо или способствовать чьей-либо деятельности

glosses: Action given to provide assistance; aid.

examples.text: I need some help with my homework.

glosses: Something or someone which provides assistance with a task.

examples.text: He was a great help to me when I was moving house.

glosses: Documentation provided with computer software that could be accessed using the computer.

examples.text: I can't find anything in the help about rotating an image.

glosses: A study aid.

examples.text: I've printed out a list of math helps.

In 1979 the Church published a Latter-day Saint edition of the King James Version of the Bible in English. Included in this edition were numerous helps to make a study of the scriptures more meaningful and rewarding.

glosses: One or more people employed to help in the maintenance of a house or the operation of a farm or enterprise.

examples.text: The help is coming round this morning to clean.
Most of the hired help is seasonal, for the harvest.

glosses: Correction of deficits, as by psychological counseling or medication or social support or remedial training.

examples.text: His suicide attempts were a cry for help.
He really needs help in handling customer complaints.
“He’s a real road-rager.” / “Yup, he really needs help, maybe anger management.”

glosses: To provide assistance to (someone or something).

examples.text: He helped his grandfather cook breakfast.

Risk is everywhere.[…]For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you. “The Norm Chronicles”[…]aims to help data-phobes find their way through this blizzard of risks.

glosses: To assist (a person) in getting something, especially food or drink at table; used with to.

examples.text: It is polite to help your guests to food before serving yourself.
Help yourself to whatever's in the fridge.

glosses: To contribute in some way to.

examples.text: The white paint on the walls helps make the room look brighter.
If you want to get a job, it helps to have some prior experience.
I've already taken three pills, but they don't seem to help my headache.

glosses: To provide assistance.

examples.text: She was struggling with the groceries, so I offered to help.
Please, help!

As soon as Julia returned with a constable, Timothy, who was on the point of exhaustion, prepared to give over to him gratefully. The newcomer turned out to be a powerful youngster, fully trained and eager to help, and he stripped off his tunic at once.

Mostly, the microbiome is beneficial. It helps with digestion and enables people to extract a lot more calories from their food than would otherwise be possible. Research over the past few years, however, has implicated it in diseases from atherosclerosis to asthma to autism.

glosses: To avoid; to prevent; to refrain from; to restrain (oneself). Usually used in nonassertive contexts with can.

examples.text: Are they going to beat us? Not if I can help it!
She never does more than she can help.
She’s trying not to smile, but she can’t help herself.
Can I help it if I'm so beautiful?
Can I help it that I fell in love with you?
We couldn’t help noticing that you were late.
We couldn’t help but notice that you were late.

glosses: To do something on the behalf of someone.

examples.text: Can you help me buy some groceries?

glosses: To assist or sympathize with (the speaker); used to express displeasure, disappointment or exasperation.

examples.text: Compare Malay tolong (“help; please”) and Hokkien 導郎 /导郎 (tō͘-lông, “help; please”)
Help lah.

glosses: A cry of distress or an urgent request for assistance.

examples.text:
— Take that, you scoundrel.
— Help! Robin, help!

glosses: A way to signal uncontrollable laughter; implying the risk of dying of laughter and needing assistance.

examples.text: helpppp that's too funny, did she rlly say that?

translations.source_sense_description: содействовать чему-либо или способствовать чьей-либо деятельности

glosses: To help.

examples.text: This book will assist you in getting your life in order.
Tutor feedback assists the learning process.

The referee seemed well placed to award the goal, but video evidence suggested the protests were well founded and the incident only strengthens the case of those lobbying for technology to assist officials.

glosses: To make a pass that leads directly towards scoring.
To help compensate for what is missing with the help of a medical technique or therapy.
To stand (at a place) or to (an opinion).

examples.text: A great part of the nobility assisted to his opinion.

glosses: To be present (at an event, occasion etc.).

examples.text: I assisted with pleasure at the representation of several tragedies and comedies.
To assist at Mass every Sunday and Holy Day of Obligation.

glosses: A helpful action or an act of giving.

examples.text: The foundation gave a much needed assist to the shelter.

glosses: The act of helping another player score points or goals
A decisive pass made to the goal scorer

examples.text: Özil has 16 assists in the Premier League and three goals; he has two more goals in the Champions League. On Monday, he took Bournemouth apart in the 2-0 win at the Emirates Stadium, setting up the first for Gabriel and scoring the second himself.

glosses: The act of helping another player score points or goals
A defensive play, allowing a teammate to record a putout.

examples.text: He had two assists in the game.

glosses: Contribuir esfuerzo o recursos para la realización de algo.

examples.text: este comedio llegaron quatro naos de Portugal, e mosén Charles rogó al capitán que le ayudase a tomarlas, por quanto heran henemigos de Françia, que ayudavan a los yngleses.

examples.text: Cómo el rey don Pedro se fue del reyno, buscando quien le ayudase, por quanto la mayor parte de los cavalleros de Castilla se alçavan contra él.

glosses: Emplear el jinete todos los medios para hacer conocer su voluntad al caballo.
